newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lukoil sees 15 pct sale 1998, oil-backed bonds 97.
newsitem.headline: Lukoil sees 15 pct sale 1998, oil-backed bonds 97.

text.p: Russian oil company LUKoil will probably delay selling a 15 percent stake earmarked for an ADR programme until next year but is likely to issue oil-backed bonds in 1997, spokesman Pyotr Neyev said on Friday.

"We will opt probably to sell the 15 percent not in 1997 but in 1998, as soon as we have the balance sheet ready," he told Reuters. He said separately: "The preliminary plan is that LUKoil in 1997 is going to issue convertible bonds... They will be convertible not into shares of LUKoil but into oil."

Neyev said delays finishing international standard accounts for 1994-1996 were holding up the sale of the 15 percent stake, which securities director Leonid Fedun in February had predicted would be sold this year in a level three American Depositary Receipt (ADR) programme requiring three years of accounts.

Privatisation Minister Alfred Kokh on Thursday reiterated he expected the 15 percent stake to be sold this year, but Neyev said the government wanted the highest possible price for the shares. "Probably what Kokh said about this year, probably he was not aware of the balance sheet situation, that's all."
Neyev said the 1997 bond would be backed by LUKoil oil exports from the Caspian Pipeline Consortium and that it would be offered to foreign investors.

He said that LUKoil had approved the plan in principal and the state privatisation committee had approved it initially but that further government approval was necessary. He declined to give further details of the bond.
